items.explanation: A barrier blocks the way, just like an obstacle. A shortcut is the opposite: it makes travel easier.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what obstacle means.

chunks.text: Her broken arm was an obstacle,
but Maya learned to write with her other hand
and finished her school project.
because it made everything much easier.

items.hint: An obstacle makes things harder, not easier.
items.explanation: The broken arm made writing hard, and Maya found a way around it. Saying it made everything easier contradicts the meaning of obstacle.

items.prompt: What was the river for the explorers?
items.passage: The explorers wanted to reach the far mountains, but a wide, rushing river stood in their way. They spent days building a raft.
items.clue: stood in their way; spent days building a raft
items.hint: The river kept them from reaching their goal.
items.explanation: The river "stood in their way" and they had to build a raft to cross it. Something that blocks a goal is an obstacle. The mountains were their goal, not the river.

words.definition: to take part in an activity or event

hero.text: Every hero participated in the clean-up day, and Juniper planted twenty new trees along the river.

words.everyday: All fifth graders will participate in the science fair by presenting an experiment to visiting families.

contrast.nonExample: Sam sat in the bleachers and watched the relay race without joining in.
contrast.explanation: Watching is not participating. To participate, you take part in the activity yourself.

items.prompt: Which person participates in the class play?

options.text: Jen plays the role of the queen.
Ray watches the play from the audience.
Mia hears about the play from her sister.

items.hint: Who takes part in the play itself?
items.explanation: Jen acts in the play, so she takes part in it. That is participating. Ray only watches.

wrong.b: Watching from the audience is not taking part in the play.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Over a thousand runners will ___ in the city marathon to raise money for the children's hospital.
items.clue: runners; in the city marathon
items.hint: The runners take part in the race.
items.explanation: Runners take part in the marathon, so they participate in it. Watch would mean they only look on.

items.prompt: Which phrase is closest in meaning to "participate" in this sentence?
items.passage: Our teacher encourages everyone to participate in class discussions, even if they feel a little shy.
items.hint: The teacher wants shy students to do more than listen.
items.explanation: Join in means to take part, which matches participate. "Even if they feel a little shy" shows the teacher wants students to speak up, not just listen.

items.prompt: Is this person participating?
items.passage: During the town meeting, Mr. Ford stood in the back hallway looking at his phone the whole time.
items.hint: Did Mr. Ford take part in the meeting?
items.explanation: Being nearby while looking at a phone is not taking part. Participating means joining in the activity.

items.prompt: Which word best describes what Grace did?
items.passage: At the community art project, Grace painted a section of the mural, helped choose colors, and cleaned brushes afterward.
items.clue: painted a section; helped choose colors; cleaned brushes
items.hint: Grace did several jobs in the project herself.
items.explanation: Painting, choosing colors, and cleaning brushes show Grace took part in the project. That is participating. Organized would mean she planned and ran it, which the passage does not say.

wrong.d: Organized means planning and running the event. Grace helped, but nothing says she was in charge.

words.definition: to keep something safe from harm or change so it lasts

hero.text: Juniper helped preserve the old forest by convincing the town to turn it into a protected park.

words.everyday: The museum keeps the ancient scrolls in cool, dark rooms to preserve the fragile paper.

contrast.nonExample: The old theater was torn down to make room for a parking lot.
contrast.explanation: Tearing something down destroys it. To preserve is to protect something so it lasts.

items.prompt: Is this an example of preserving?
items.passage: Grandma pressed the wedding flowers inside a heavy book so they would stay pretty for many years.
items.hint: Did Grandma do something to make the flowers last?
items.explanation: Pressing the flowers keeps them from rotting so they last for years. Keeping something safe so it lasts is preserving.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Long before refrigerators, people used salt and smoke to ___ meat through the winter months.
items.clue: before refrigerators; through the winter months
items.hint: Refrigerators keep food from going bad. What did salt and smoke do?
items.explanation: Salt and smoke kept meat from rotting so it lasted "through the winter". That is preserving. Spoil is the opposite.

wrong.c: Serve means to give food to people. The clue is about making it last.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "preserve" in this sentence?
items.passage: Volunteers are working to preserve the wetlands where thousands of birds stop to rest each spring.
items.hint: Preserve means to keep safe. What is the opposite?
items.explanation: Destroy means to ruin completely, the opposite of preserve. Protect is a synonym.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what preserve means.

chunks.text: To preserve the old letters,
the librarian sealed them
in special acid-free folders.
and left them out in the rain.

items.hint: Preserving keeps something safe so it lasts.
items.explanation: Sealing the letters in special folders protects them, which is preserving. Leaving them in the rain would ruin them.

items.prompt: What is the town trying to do with its oldest buildings?
items.passage: The town passed a law that its 200-year-old buildings cannot be torn down, and owners must repair them using the original style.
items.clue: cannot be torn down; repair them using the original style
items.hint: The law protects the buildings and keeps them the same.
items.explanation: Keeping buildings from being "torn down" and repairing them in "the original style" protects them from harm and change. That is preserving.

words.definition: to officially say that something is not allowed

hero.text: The academy rules prohibit flying inside the library, so Kai walked quietly between the shelves.

words.everyday: Many beaches prohibit glass bottles because broken glass can hurt people walking barefoot.

contrast.nonExample: The pool allows swimmers to bring snacks and drinks onto the deck.
contrast.explanation: Allowing something is the opposite of prohibiting it. Prohibit means a rule says you may not.

items.prompt: What does "prohibits" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The national park prohibits feeding the bears, and anyone who does it can be fined.
items.hint: People who do it can be fined. Is it allowed?
items.explanation: Getting fined shows feeding bears is against the rules. Prohibit means a rule says something is not allowed.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Our school rules ___ phones during class, so students must keep them in their lockers until the last bell.
items.clue: must keep them in their lockers
items.hint: If phones must stay in lockers, are they allowed in class?
items.explanation: Keeping phones "in their lockers" means students cannot use them in class. The rules prohibit them. Allow and require mean the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "prohibited" in this sentence?
items.passage: In 1920, a new law in the United States prohibited selling alcohol anywhere in the country.
items.hint: Which word means a law said it could not be done at all?
items.explanation: Banned means officially not allowed, which matches prohibited. Discouraged is weaker: it means people were urged not to, but it was not against the law.

wrong.d: Discouraged is weaker than prohibited. A law that prohibits makes something not allowed at all.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: The sign does not just suggest that you stay off the ice; it ___ skating there, and guards enforce the rule.
items.clue: does not just suggest; guards enforce the rule
items.hint: It's stronger than a suggestion. Which word means an official rule against it?
items.explanation: "Does not just suggest" and "guards enforce the rule" show this is an official ban. Prohibits is the strongest fit. Discourages is only a suggestion.

items.prompt: Which line uses "prohibit" correctly?

options.text: "I prohibit pancakes for breakfast every Sunday."
"The zoo's rules prohibit tapping on the glass."

items.hint: Prohibit is used for rules that say something is not allowed.
items.explanation: Zoo rules that say you may not tap on the glass prohibit it. The other lines use prohibit like eat, lend, or hop.

words.definition: to suggest something as a good choice

hero.text: Pixel recommended the northern route because it was shorter and had fewer storms, so the team chose it.

words.everyday: The librarian recommended a mystery series to me, and I finished the first book in two days.

contrast.nonExample: Ava told her friend never to eat at the new diner because the food was cold.
contrast.explanation: Warning someone away is the opposite of recommending. To recommend is to suggest something as a good choice.

items.prompt: Which person is recommending something?

options.text: Lin says, "You should try the art club. I think you'd love it."

items.hint: Who is suggesting something as a good choice?
items.explanation: Lin suggests the art club because she thinks her friend would love it. That is recommending. Mom gives an order, which is different from a suggestion.

wrong.d: Mom is giving an order, not suggesting a good choice.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Dentists ___ brushing your teeth twice a day to keep them strong and free of cavities.
items.clue: to keep them strong and free of cavities
items.hint: Dentists think brushing is a good idea. What do they do?
items.explanation: Brushing keeps teeth healthy, so dentists suggest it as a good choice. That is recommending. Forbid means the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "recommended" in this sentence?
items.passage: The park ranger recommended that we bring extra water because the trail has no fountains.
items.hint: The ranger gave helpful advice.
items.explanation: Advised means gave a suggestion about what to do, which matches recommended. Promised would mean the ranger guaranteed something.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what recommend means.

chunks.text: I recommend the bean tacos
at the food truck
because they are fresh and delicious.
because they made me feel sick.

items.hint: When you recommend something, you give a good reason to try it.
items.explanation: "Fresh and delicious" is a reason to suggest the tacos. Feeling sick would be a reason to warn people away, not recommend.

items.prompt: What did the coach do?
items.passage: The coach told Jada's parents that she was ready for the advanced team and suggested they sign her up this spring.
items.clue: ready for the advanced team; suggested they sign her up
items.hint: The coach suggested a good choice for Jada.
items.explanation: The coach "suggested they sign her up" because she was ready. Suggesting something as a good choice is recommending.

words.definition: to refuse to accept, believe, or agree to something

hero.text: Nova rejected the villain's offer of gold, saying she would never trade the city's safety for riches.

words.everyday: The scientists rejected the idea that the Earth was flat after sailors traveled all the way around it.

contrast.nonExample: Tom happily accepted the invitation to his cousin's birthday party.
contrast.explanation: Accepting is the opposite of rejecting. To reject means to refuse or say no to something.

items.prompt: Is this an example of rejecting?
items.passage: The class voted on the new field trip plan, and almost every student cheered and said yes to it.
items.hint: Did the class refuse the plan or accept it?
items.explanation: The students said yes, so they accepted the plan. Rejecting means refusing to accept something, so this does not fit.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The judges had to ___ the robot because it was larger than the size limit in the contest rules.
items.clue: larger than the size limit
items.hint: The robot broke a rule. What would the judges do?
items.explanation: Breaking the size rule means the judges could not accept the robot. They had to reject it. Accept is the opposite.

items.prompt: Which phrase is closest in meaning to "rejected" in this sentence?
items.passage: The publisher rejected the author's first story, but she kept writing and sold her tenth one.
items.hint: "But she kept writing" tells you the first story did not succeed.
items.explanation: Turned down means refused, which matches rejected. "But she kept writing" shows the publisher said no to her first story.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: After looking at the evidence carefully, the scientist decided to ___ her old theory and start over with a new one.
items.clue: start over with a new one
items.hint: She is starting over. What did she do with the old theory?
items.explanation: Starting over with a new theory means she no longer accepted the old one. She rejected it. Defend would mean she kept supporting it.

items.prompt: Which word best describes what the kitten did with the new food?
items.passage: Every time Marcus filled the bowl with the new food, the kitten sniffed it, turned away, and walked off.
items.clue: sniffed it, turned away, and walked off
items.hint: Did the kitten accept the food?
items.explanation: Turning away and walking off "every time" shows the kitten refused the food. That is rejecting. Devoured would mean it ate it all hungrily.

words.definition: the order in which things happen or are arranged

hero.text: Bolt pressed the buttons in the correct sequence, red then blue then green, and the vault door slid open.

words.everyday: To retell a story, list the events in sequence: what happened first, next, and last.

contrast.nonExample: Max tossed all the comic panels in a pile, so nobody could tell what happened first.
contrast.explanation: A jumbled pile has no order. A sequence is the order in which things happen.

items.prompt: What does "sequence" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The life cycle of a frog follows a sequence: egg, tadpole, froglet, and then adult frog.
items.hint: Look at the list after the colon. What do you notice?
items.explanation: Egg, tadpole, froglet, and adult happen one after another in order. A sequence is the order in which things happen.

items.prompt: Sequence can mean "the order things happen in", "a list of numbers that follows a pattern", or "one scene in a movie". Which meaning is used here?
items.passage: In math class, we studied the sequence 3, 6, 9, 12 and figured out that the next number would be 15.

options.text: a list of numbers that follows a pattern
the steps for a science experiment

items.clue: In math class; 3, 6, 9, 12; the next number
items.hint: Look at the numbers and the subject: math.
items.explanation: "In math class" and the numbers 3, 6, 9, 12 show that sequence here means a list of numbers following a pattern (add 3). It is still about order, used in a math way.

wrong.b: A movie sequence is a set of scenes. This passage is about numbers in math class.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The recipe only works if you follow the steps in the right ___, adding the eggs before the flour.
items.clue: the eggs before the flour
items.hint: "Before" tells you the order matters.
items.explanation: "Adding the eggs before the flour" is about order. Following the steps in the right sequence means doing them in order.

wrong.d: Amount is about how much, but the clue "before" is about order.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what sequence means.

chunks.text: The timeline shows the sequence of events,
starting with the first settlers in 1620
and ending with statehood in 1788.
with all the dates mixed up randomly.

items.hint: A sequence goes in order, from first to last.
items.explanation: Starting with 1620 and ending with 1788 puts the events in order, which is a sequence. Mixed-up dates have no order.

items.prompt: What does "sequence" mean as used in this passage?
items.passage: The best part of the film was the chase sequence. For five minutes, the camera followed the horses racing through the canyon.

options.text: a part of a movie showing one event

items.clue: film; for five minutes, the camera followed
items.hint: This passage is about a movie, not math.
items.explanation: "Film" and "the camera followed" show that sequence here means a section of a movie with connected shots of one event. It is a series of shots in order.

words.definition: important or large enough to be noticed and to matter

hero.text: Finding the hidden water pipe leak was a significant discovery, because it saved the town thousands of gallons each day.

words.everyday: The invention of the printing press was a significant event in history because it spread books and ideas widely.

contrast.nonExample: The temperature changed from 70 degrees to 71 degrees between lunch and recess.
contrast.explanation: A one-degree change is too small to matter much. Significant means important or large enough to matter.

items.prompt: Is this a significant event?
items.passage: The first person to walk on the moon changed how the whole world thought about space travel.
items.hint: Did this event matter a lot?
items.explanation: An event that "changed how the whole world thought" is very important. That is significant.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Reading every night made ___ changes in Kofi's test scores, which jumped from Cs to As in one year.
items.clue: jumped from Cs to As
items.hint: Going from Cs to As is a big change or a small one?
items.explanation: Scores that "jumped from Cs to As" show a large, important change. That is significant. Tiny is the opposite.

items.prompt: "Insignificant" adds the prefix "in-" to "significant". What does "insignificant" mean?
items.hint: The prefix in- here means "not", like in incorrect.
items.explanation: In- means not, so insignificant means not important, the opposite of significant. In- does not mean inside here.

wrong.c: In- can mean inside in some words, but in insignificant it means not.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "significant" in this sentence?
items.passage: The cleanup project had a significant effect on the river, and fish returned for the first time in decades.
items.hint: Fish returned after decades. Was the effect big or small?
items.explanation: Major means large and important, which matches significant. Fish returning after decades shows a big effect.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the role of the Underground Railroad in history?
items.passage: The Underground Railroad helped thousands of enslaved people escape to freedom, and its stories still inspire people today.
items.clue: helped thousands; still inspire people today
items.hint: It helped many people and still matters today.
items.explanation: Helping "thousands" escape and still inspiring people "today" show the Underground Railroad was very important. That is significant.

words.definition: to tell only the most important points in a short way

hero.text: After the long mission, Rex summarized what happened in three sentences so the mayor understood it right away.

words.everyday: To summarize the chapter, Lila wrote the main problem, the key events, and how it ended in one paragraph.

contrast.nonExample: Asked about the movie, Ben retold every single scene in order for forty-five minutes.
contrast.explanation: Retelling every detail is not summarizing. A summary is short and includes only the most important points.

items.prompt: Which student summarizes the story of "The Three Little Pigs"?

options.text: "Three pigs built houses. The wolf blew down two, but the brick one kept them safe."
"The first pig had a pink nose and wore a red hat on Tuesday."

items.hint: A summary tells the main events in a short way.
items.explanation: Option a tells the most important events in two short sentences. That is a summary. Option b gives small details, not the main points.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Since we had only one minute left, Ms. Grant asked us to ___ the article in a single sentence.
items.clue: only one minute left; in a single sentence
items.hint: With little time and one sentence, you can share only the main idea.
items.explanation: "One minute" and "a single sentence" mean telling just the main point briefly. That is summarizing. Elaborate means adding more detail, the opposite.

wrong.b: Elaborate means adding details, but there was only time for one sentence.

items.prompt: Which phrase is closest in meaning to "summarize" in this sentence?
items.passage: At the end of the meeting, the club president will summarize the decisions we made today.
items.hint: At the end of a meeting, a leader often briefly repeats the main points.
items.explanation: Sum up means to state the main points briefly, which matches summarize. Writing down every word is the opposite of a short summary.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: The news reporter had only thirty seconds, so she had to ___ the long city council meeting for viewers.
items.clue: only thirty seconds; long
items.hint: A long meeting, very little time. Which choice is short?
items.explanation: With "only thirty seconds" for a "long" meeting, she had to give just the main points. That is summarizing. Explaining fully would take far too long.

items.prompt: What did Felix do?
items.passage: Felix read a ten-page article about volcanoes. Then he wrote: "Volcanoes form where melted rock escapes Earth's crust, and they can build mountains or destroy towns."
items.clue: ten-page article; one sentence with the main points
items.hint: Ten pages became one sentence with the main ideas.
items.explanation: Felix turned ten pages into one sentence with the most important points. That is summarizing. He did not copy it or make it sound bigger.

words.definition: as much as is needed; enough

hero.text: Kai checked that the shelter had sufficient blankets for every family before the snowstorm hit that night.

words.everyday: Plants need sufficient sunlight to make food; without enough light, their leaves turn pale and weak.

contrast.nonExample: There were twenty-five students but only twelve chairs, so many had to stand.
contrast.explanation: Twelve chairs for twenty-five students is not enough. Sufficient means as much as is needed.

items.prompt: Is there a sufficient amount?
items.passage: Mom baked twenty-four cupcakes for a class of thirty students.
items.hint: Will every student get a cupcake?
items.explanation: Twenty-four cupcakes for thirty students leaves six students without one. That is not sufficient. Sufficient means enough for what is needed.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The judge said there was not ___ evidence to prove the man had taken the bike, so he was set free.
items.clue: to prove; so he was set free
items.hint: The man was freed because there wasn't enough of something.
items.explanation: He was set free because the evidence was not enough "to prove" he took the bike. Sufficient means enough.

items.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "sufficient" in this sentence?
items.passage: Two hours should be sufficient time to finish the hike and get back before dark.
items.hint: Sufficient doesn't mean a lot extra, just the amount needed.
items.explanation: Enough means as much as is needed, which matches sufficient. Extra means more than needed, which is a slightly different idea.

wrong.a: Extra means more than you need. Sufficient means just enough.

items.prompt: The prefix "in-" means "not". If a plant gets insufficient water, what is happening?

options.text: It gets just the right amount of water.
It gets water inside its pot.
It does not get enough water.

items.hint: In- + sufficient = not enough.
items.explanation: In- means not, so insufficient means not enough. A plant with insufficient water is not getting the amount it needs.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the food the hikers packed?
items.passage: The hikers packed food for three days. Their trip lasted exactly three days, and they finished their last snack on the drive home.
items.clue: food for three days; exactly three days
items.hint: Did the hikers have too little, too much, or just enough?
items.explanation: The food lasted exactly as long as the trip, so they had just enough. That is sufficient. Excessive would mean far too much, and insufficient would mean not enough.

words.definition: a picture, object, or sign that stands for something else

hero.text: The lightning bolt on Bolt's chest is a symbol of his speed and the energy he brings to every rescue.

words.everyday: The dove is often used as a symbol of peace in paintings, posters, and flags.

contrast.nonExample: Jen drew a picture of her real dog, Max, sleeping on the couch.
contrast.explanation: A picture of the actual dog just shows the dog. A symbol stands for a different idea, like a heart standing for love.

items.prompt: What does "symbol" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: In math, the plus sign is a symbol that tells you to add two numbers together.

options.text: a sign that stands for something

items.hint: The plus sign tells you what to do. It stands for an idea.
items.explanation: The plus sign stands for the idea of adding. A symbol is a sign or picture that stands for something else.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The bald eagle was chosen as a national ___ of the United States because it stands for strength and freedom.
items.clue: stands for strength and freedom
items.hint: Something that "stands for" an idea is called what?
items.explanation: "Stands for strength and freedom" tells you the eagle represents ideas. That makes it a symbol.

items.prompt: In this story, what is the lantern a symbol of?
items.passage: Every night during the war, Grandma left a lantern glowing in her window. She said it would stay lit until her son came home safely.
items.clue: stay lit until her son came home safely
items.hint: Why did Grandma keep the lantern lit? What was she waiting for?
items.explanation: The lantern stayed lit "until her son came home safely", so it stands for her hope that he would return. An object that stands for an idea is a symbol.

wrong.a: The lantern was not about the dark; it was about waiting for her son.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what symbol means.

chunks.text: On a map,
a small tent is a symbol
that stands for a campground.
that has no meaning at all.

items.hint: A symbol always stands for something.
items.explanation: The tent picture stands for a campground, so it is a symbol. A symbol with "no meaning at all" would not be a symbol.

items.prompt: Which line uses "symbol" correctly?

options.text: "I'll symbol you at the bus stop."
"My lunch was a big symbol of noodles."
"In our flag, the star is a symbol of unity."

items.hint: Watch out: cymbal (the drum instrument) sounds the same but is spelled differently.
items.explanation: A star that stands for unity is a symbol. Option b needs cymbal, a brass instrument, which sounds the same but means something completely different.

wrong.b: This should be cymbal, the round brass instrument. It sounds like symbol but has a different meaning.

words.definition: to put something in danger, or to be a sign that something bad may happen

hero.text: Rising floodwater threatened the farm animals, so Juniper and Rex led them up to the high hill.

words.everyday: Pollution in the ocean threatens sea turtles, which can mistake plastic bags for jellyfish.

contrast.nonExample: The gentle spring rain watered the gardens and filled the birdbaths.
contrast.explanation: Gentle rain helps rather than harms. To threaten is to put something in danger.

items.prompt: What does "threatens" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: Cutting down the rainforest threatens thousands of animals that depend on the trees for food and shelter.
items.hint: The animals depend on the trees. What happens to them if the trees are cut down?
items.explanation: The animals need the trees, so cutting them down puts the animals in danger. That is what threatens means here.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Dark gray clouds ___ to ruin our picnic, so we packed up the food and headed for the car.
items.clue: Dark gray clouds; packed up the food
items.hint: The clouds were a sign that something bad might happen.
items.explanation: Dark clouds were a sign that rain might ruin the picnic, so they threatened it. Threaten can mean being a warning sign of something bad.

wrong.a: Promised is usually for good things. The clouds signaled something bad.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "threatened" in this sentence?
items.passage: A long drought threatened the town's water supply, and people were asked to stop watering lawns.
items.hint: Threaten means to put in danger. What means to keep safe?
items.explanation: Protected means kept safe, the opposite of threatened. Endangered is a synonym.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what threaten means.

chunks.text: The wildfire threatened
homes at the edge of the forest,
so families were told to leave quickly.
so families stayed and had a barbecue.

items.hint: When something threatens you, there is danger.
items.explanation: A wildfire putting homes in danger would make families leave. Staying for a barbecue does not match the danger in threatened.

items.prompt: Which word best describes what the beetles are doing to the trees?
items.passage: Tiny beetles have spread through the pine forest. They bore into the bark, and many trees could die within a few years.
items.clue: bore into the bark; many trees could die
items.hint: The beetles might cause the trees to die.
items.explanation: "Many trees could die" shows the beetles put the forest in danger. That is threatening. Threaten does not always mean someone says a threat; it can mean causing danger.
